groups.name: Attachment
groups.description: This group is based on the 'Attachment' schema file and covers all database entities related to the management of uploaded files and attachments in the platform. The primary tables are shopping_mall_ai_attachments, shopping_mall_ai_attachment_versions, and shopping_mall_ai_attachment_business_links. The 'shopping_mall_ai_attachments' table is the master metadata for all uploaded files, including images, documents, invoices, and compliance-related files, with fields for uploader, file name, MIME type, storage URI, size, business domain, retention policy, legal hold status, deleted flag, access control, and timestamps. The 'shopping_mall_ai_attachment_versions' table manages immutable versioning of each attachment, tracking modifications, version number, file URI, file size, timestamps, and notes on the difference/changes per version, along with deletion status. The 'shopping_mall_ai_attachment_business_links' table links attachments to business entities by domain and target ID for traceability, usage, and referential integrity, including the linking user and creation time. Key operations for this group include CRUD on attachments, management of attachment versions (including restore and audit), and business-domain links to associate files to entities such as products, reviews, or invoices. Relationships within this group are strictly hierarchical: an attachment can have multiple versions, and each attachment can be linked to multiple business entities via the links table. Functional requirements covered by this group include file upload, metadata/query/search, retrieval via CDN URIs, compliance/retention enforcement, evidence preservation, access control, and linkage to domain entities. The group supports workflows for upload (with validation), versioning, linkage, retrieval, legal hold management, and explicit soft/hard deletion, mapping directly to the file/business domain asset management needs described in requirements and in the ShoppingMallAi platform's compliance and business processes.

Used in scenarios where a file is re-uploaded for correction, update, or as part of audit/evidence flow.

Only the original uploader, authorized administrator, or compliance/legal role can register a new version. Creating a version does not overwrite prior versions; full chain of custody and evidence audit is guaranteed.

Input fields include file URI, file size, version number, modifier (user), and diff comment explaining the change. The operation enforces all business rules for attachment and version domain, audit context, and compliance requirements. Failure scenarios include unauthorized version changes, violations of legal hold, or attempts on deleted/locked attachments. All changes are audit logged per system compliance.

New versioning is typically initiated after a physical upload or when an administrator, original uploader, or compliance officer needs to update/correct the file while preserving the chain of custody.

Input includes the file URI, size, modifier (user), version number, and a comment describing changes/differences vs. previous version. The operation enforces version increment integrity, attachment ACL, and legal hold compliance.

Only applicable roles may register a version for attachments they have rights to. Business and regulatory rules dictate handling of active, deleted, or legally-restricted files. The new version is immutably appended — prior versions remain accessible for authorized audit. Use cases: correction after error, legal evidence submission, catalog asset update.

IPageIShoppingMallAiAttachment.ISummary.description:
A paginated result set containing summary data for search/filter results over attachment records in the platform. Used in all GET/PATCH /attachments list-style endpoints, with strong business relevance for compliance and asset management.

This schema includes two properties: pagination (IPage.IPagination) for page navigation, and data (array of IShoppingMallAiAttachment.ISummary) for the actual records. Complete for attachment list workflows.

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the attachment. This is the primary key of the attachment record and is required for linking, auditing, and further operations.

filename.description: The original file name at time of upload. May be displayed in UI or used for audit purposes.

mime_type.description: The standard MIME type for the file (e.g., image/png, application/pdf). Used for file handling, preview, and compliance.

file_size.description: File size in bytes. Used for quota management, performance optimization, and audit trails.

business_domain.description: A string code representing the business domain/purpose for the attachment (e.g., 'product_image', 'invoice', 'evidence', 'compliance_doc'). Important for filtering and domain-specific workflows.

retention_policy_code.description: Specifies the retention/compliance policy code for this file. Used for determining purge, archive, and audit windows.

legal_hold.description: Indicates if this attachment is under legal hold, which means it cannot be deleted or modified until compliance review. True if under legal hold, otherwise false.

deleted.description: True if the attachment has been logically deleted (soft delete). Logical deletions remove the file from UI and API usage except for compliance roles.

uploaded_by_id.description: UUID referencing the user (customer, seller, or admin) who uploaded the attachment. Used for access control and audit purposes. Display/export of this field must follow business policy and context. It should never be supplied by the client and is only shown in summary responses if the business context allows, to support compliance/audit requirements.

created_at.description: Timestamp of upload/attachment creation in ISO 8601 format. Used for sorting and audit.

IShoppingMallAiAttachment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an attachment file managed by the shoppingMallAi platform. Contains only non-sensitive, business-relevant, or compliance-filtered fields suitable for list/search display, not the full attachment or all detailed audit fields.

This schema is used in paginated attachment listings, search responses, and summary cards, and is designed to balance discoverability with compliance and privacy filtering.

pagination.description: Page information for the attachment version summary list result. Contains current page, limit per page, total records, and total pages. Always present for API and UI navigation.

data.description: List of IShoppingMallAiAttachmentVersion.ISummary objects. Each holds summary information for a version of an attachment (file), suitable for display and audit navigation.

IPageIShoppingMallAiAttachmentVersion.IS.description:

Includes both the page navigation data (IPage.IPagination) and the results array (data), which is an array of IShoppingMallAiAttachmentVersion.ISummary entries, filtered, sorted, and truncated per the incoming query.

id.description: The unique ID (UUID) of the version/snapshot record. Required for version navigation, audit, and referencing specific file states.

attachment_id.description: The UUID of the parent attachment to which this version belongs, for relational and traceability purposes.

version_number.description: Monotonically increasing version number. Indicates history order (1=original, incremented per subsequent upload/change).

file_uri.description: Storage URI (internal or CDN) where this particular version is stored. Used for download/access by eligible roles and for integrity checks.

file_size.description: The size of this version's file in bytes. Returned for information, quota calculation, and change audit.

oneOf.description: Optional commentary or annotation explaining this version, such as 'fix metadata field', 'format corrected', etc. May be null if no diff.comment was provided.

IShoppingMallAiAttachmentVersion.ISummar.description:

This type is designed for compliance, UI history views, and page-level displays, not for complete file or chain-of-custody representation.
